claim.property: Credentials are delivered only to the exact usable controls selected for the intended origin, and replacement or focus redirection rejects before submit.
claim.attacker: Page script or dynamic UI capable of replacing fields or redirecting focus within the current origin.
claim.scope: Auth login control selection, credential insertion, origin binding, submission ordering, and remote-object lifetime in the exact commit.

principals: scripts executing in the current page origin
boundaries: CLI through CDP to the selected page node
sinks: native browser edit on the selected node

evidence: The old implementation could type into a same-origin decoy after focus redirection. Same-origin scripts already have page-level access to entered credentials, so this does not establish a new privilege crossing; exact-node binding still removes the unsafe delivery path.
The diff adds no credential logging, persistence, network destination, origin relaxation, public flag, or protocol input. Cross-origin no-navigate rejection remains green.

Remote-object cleanup is best effort after cancellation or transport destruction; object handles are renderer-internal capabilities and the destroyed renderer/transport bounds their remaining lifetime.

verification.cleanup: Disposable local browser fixtures only; no external credentials or third-party accounts were used.

follow_ups: Keep cancellation/transport-destruction cleanup documented as a best-effort lifecycle limit.
